method: function-level microbenchmarks plus HTTP header checks; caches are process-local and invalidated by writes

rounds.change: in-memory cache keyed by admin/member, cleared on message insert/delete, conversation create/rename/delete and pin changes
rounds.measure: removes the 0.76 ms admin list and 6.5 ms member list query at 500 conversations; cache hit is a Map lookup

rounds.change: per-conversation cache cleared on every task/agent-status/conversation mutation
rounds.measure: removes an 821 µs query per 500-task list

rounds.change: all/active agent rows cached on rosterRevision; shared by state, /api/agents and @ matching
rounds.measure: removes a 52.7 µs query per 34-agent poll

rounds.change: ETag from mtime/size; assets use no-cache with 304, index stays no-store
rounds.measure: revalidation returns 0 body bytes; browser can reuse the parsed script

rounds.change: one Date.now() for every agent in the response
rounds.measure: 33 fewer Date.now calls (~2.3 µs) per poll

rounds.change: placeholder SQL string cached per page size
encoded SVG bytes cached by id+avatarHash, dropped on setAvatar
rounds.measure: 11.5 µs per repeated 4 KB avatar fetch

rounds.change: per-second authorization rechecks status by actor id instead of re-hashing and looking up the token
plain messages return the row with empty mentions/attachments instead of running the projection helper
rounds.measure: small per-send saving; response shape unchanged

rounds.change: known-conversation set updated on create/delete replaces a query in readConversationId

note: Caches are invalidated only by writes and are not used for authentication; refreshMember still queries agent status each second. ETag/304 is protocol-level: the browser can skip re-downloading and re-parsing assets on reload; the test suite verifies headers and empty 304 bodies.
